title: External public-data validation
not_a_milestone: This is not a LayerProof milestone. The accepted Week 1–8 results are unchanged.
question: Does LayerProof's scientific, domain-support and abstention framework behave sensibly on independent real asphalt datasets outside the original SPARC soil/UGM trial?

method.models: Ordinary least squares, ridge (alpha 1.0) and a random forest (200 trees) — the accepted baselines, unchanged and untuned
method.row_level_label: EXPLORATORY ROW-LEVEL ANALYSIS — NOT INDEPENDENT EXTERNAL VALIDATION
method.rule: A relationship is called stable only if its direction is the same in every source group with at least 10 records in every dataset, and the one-input linear model beats the mean in every grouped design. Random-row results and publication-reported metrics never count.

datasets.source_publication_methods: The publication reports CatBoost, SVR and random-forest models tuned with Bayesian optimisation, and uses NDG density as an input when predicting core density. Those results are characteristics of the source and are not LayerProof validation.

HMV does not occur in the accepted evidence (CMV and CCV).
No accepted reference range exists for HMV.
Passes 1–18.5, mostly fractional; accepted reference passes are 2–4 (soil) and 2, 4, 8 (UGM), as integers.
Not stated.
38.5–98.9 °C; the accepted evidence has no temperature field.
2.3–8.8 km/h; speed is not part of the accepted reference domain.
Not present.
18.8–67 Hz, mostly near 65 Hz; the accepted evidence was filtered to 29–31 Hz.
NDG exists as a modality in the accepted evidence, but here as relative density (%Gmm) rather than dry density (t/m³). Core density is a modality the accepted evidence does not contain.
ID labels only; no coordinates, CRS or documented geometry.
Every row carries two physical values, but independent locations cannot be established.

limitations: Processed, aggregated values; no raw records.
No project, site or coordinate information.
HMV is not defined in the supplied files.
One record looks column-shifted in the source.
Licence not stated, so the records are not redistributed.

reasons: No compaction measurement value is shared: Asphalt A has CMV, CCV, AICV and RMV; Asphalt B has HMV.
The physical targets differ: NNDG without a unit, against NDG and core density in %Gmm.
Neither can be compared numerically with the accepted SPARC evidence: different material, nuclear-gauge dry density in t/m³, and roller values summarised differently.

frozen_sparc_reference.note: Read for comparison only; not recomputed.

abstention.reason: No baseline holds up across the grouped designs, and no independent project or site exists to validate one.
Without a model that has passed validation there is no credible predictive uncertainty.
All holdouts are inside one dataset; projects and sites are not identified.
No coordinates, CRS or location geometry.
Different material, measurement values and physical targets from the accepted evidence.
NNDG (unit not stated), NDG %Gmm and core %Gmm are different quantities from each other and from accepted dry density in t/m³.
PUBLISHED_AGGREGATED_REAL roller values do not satisfy the accepted REAL_IC check, which needs row-level REAL_FIELD observations.

interpretation_labels.label: CROSS-DATASET RELATIONSHIP NOT STABLE
interpretation_labels.why: The direction of the HMV–density association differs between layer-thickness groups in Asphalt B, and the one-input model is worse than the mean when a thickness group is held out. Asphalt A shows a positive within-dataset association. The declared stability rule is not met.

interpretation_labels.label: EXTERNAL DOMAIN SHIFT OBSERVED
interpretation_labels.why: Both datasets differ from the accepted evidence in material, measurement values and physical target; Asphalt A's CCV values lie entirely outside the accepted reference range.

interpretation_labels.label: EXTERNAL RELATIONSHIP OBSERVED BUT INDEPENDENT VALIDATION LIMITED
interpretation_labels.why: Applies to Asphalt A only: a positive association between its ICMVs and NNDG, with modest grouped R² inside one dataset and mixed results on the source's own validation file.

interpretation_labels.label: INSUFFICIENT METADATA FOR INDEPENDENT EXTERNAL VALIDATION
interpretation_labels.why: Neither dataset identifies projects, sites or coordinates.

interpretation_labels.label: CROSS-DATASET PREDICTIVE TRANSFER NOT COMPARABLE
interpretation_labels.why: No shared measurement value or target; no transfer test was run.

interpretation_labels.label: EXTERNAL SUPPORT FOR ABSTENTION FRAMEWORK
interpretation_labels.why: The accepted evidence gate did not allow a scientific claim for either dataset, and the grouped results show why: relationships that look usable on random rows weaken or reverse when a source group is held out. This is consistent with abstaining; it is two datasets, not a proof.

not_assessable: SPATIAL CANDIDATE PRIORITIZATION NOT ASSESSABLE FROM THIS DATASET

answers.q: Did the independent asphalt datasets show a stable universal ICMV-density relationship?
answers.a: No. Asphalt A shows a positive association inside one dataset. In Asphalt B the direction of the HMV–density association changes between layer-thickness groups.

answers.q: Did performance or relationship strength differ materially across datasets?
answers.a: Yes. One-input grouped R² is about +0.16 to +0.27 in Asphalt A and from about −1.75 to +0.22 in Asphalt B, depending on the target and on how records are held out.

answers.q: Did LayerProof's abstention and domain-support logic behave appropriately?
answers.a: Yes, on this evidence. The accepted gate allowed no scientific claim for either dataset, both are out of domain relative to the accepted evidence, and the grouped results do not contradict that.

answers.q: What additional claim, if any, can LayerProof now make?
answers.a: That it has been examined on two independent public asphalt datasets, that no stable universal relationship between compaction measurement values and density was found, and that its evidence gate withheld a scientific claim for both.
Predicting density or stiffness; validity across materials; transfer between datasets; any benefit of the candidate ranking; any field performance.

answers.q: What still requires GPS-located independent spatial data?
answers.a: Any evaluation of verification-candidate ranking or of where to test next, and any spatial evidence-support analysis, on data other than SPARC.

answers.q: What still requires prospective field validation?
answers.a: Whether candidates raised by LayerProof help an engineer place tests where they add evidence on a live project.

public_statement: Across two independent public asphalt datasets, compaction measurements did not show a stable universal relationship with physical density. LayerProof therefore keeps evidence specific to its context and abstains when transfer is unsupported.
